asrMetadata.note: Native tiling is 3 tiles of 14 frames with 13 frames lookahead; a 2240 ms call processes 28 encoder frames. This matches the installed artifact, not the older [56, 0] documentation.

componentLoadFreshProcessSeconds.probe: tools/profile-coreml-load.swift, release binary, separate process per row, same path and signing identity

encoder.all: timed out after 600 s; not pursued

observations: The encoder owns almost all model load time; decoder, joint and decoder_joint are under 4 ms each.
Warm CPU specialization is cached across processes (6 ms) while the GPU path still pays 0.78-1.59 s per fresh process, so a resident process is the only current way to avoid that cost.
First-ever CPU specialization was 6.79 s, so the 6 ms rows are cache hits, not a faster weight read.
ANE specialization cost 140-370 s per fresh process on this machine, so the vendor's ANE recommendation is unusable for launch-time loading here; the GPU product default stands.

The manager honors the passed MLModelConfiguration and already exposes per-model overrides (FLUIDAUDIO_ENCODER_CU, FLUIDAUDIO_DECODER_CU, FLUIDAUDIO_JOINT_CU, FLUIDAUDIO_DECODERJOINT_CU) plus SUPERFLOW_COMPUTE_UNITS, so Phase 2 needs no loader change.

The vendor loads decoder.mlmodelc and joint.mlmodelc whenever present even if decoder_joint.mlmodelc covers the path; measured cost is under 4 ms each, so skipping them is not worth a dependency patch.
